annotations.title: Chaire of Moyſes.
annotations.text: ◦ God preſerueth the truth of Chriſtian religion in the Apoſtolike See of Rome, which is in the new law anſwerable to the chaire of Moyſes, notwithſtanding the Biſhops of the ſame were neuer ſo wicked of life: yea though ſome traitour as il as Iudas were Biſhop thereof, it ſhould not be preiudicial to the Church and innocent Chriſtians, for whom our Lord prouiding ſaid, Doe that which they ſay, but doe not as they doe. Auguſt. Epiſt. 165.

notes.text: The See of Rome preserued in truth.

annotations.title: Whatſoeuer they ſhal ſay.
annotations.text: [1] Why (ſaith S. Auguſtin [2] ) doeſt thou call the Apoſtolic Chaire the chaire of peſtilence? If for the men, why? Did our Lord Jeſus Chriſt for the Phariſees, any wrong to the Chaire wherein they ſate? Did he not commend that chaire of Moyſes, and preſeruing the honour of the chaire, reproue them? For he ſaith: They ſitte vpon the Chaire of Moyſes, that which they ſay, do ye. Theſe things if you did vvel conſider, you vvould not for the men whom you defame, blaſpheme the See Apoſtolic, wherewith you do not communicate. And againe he ſaith [3]: Neither for the Phariſees (to whom you compare vs not of vviſdom but of malice) did our Lord command the Chaire of Moyſes to be forſaken, in vvhich chaire verily he figured his owne. For he vvarneth the people to do that which they ſay, and not to do that which they do, and that the holineſſe of the Chaire be in no caſe forſaken, nor the vnity of the flocke divided, for the naughty Paſtors.

notes.text: The dignitie of the See of Rome, notwithstanding some euil Bishops thereof.

annotations.title: Loue the firſt places.
annotations.text: He condemneth not dew places of Superiority geuen or taken of men according to their degrees, but ambitious ſeeking for the ſame, and their prowde hart and wicked intention, which he ſaw within them, and therfore might boldly reprehend them.

annotations.title: One is your maiſter.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> In the Catholike Church there is one Maiſter, Chriſt our Lord, and vnder him one Vicar, with whom al Catholike Doctors and teachers are one, becauſe they teach al one thing. but in Arch-heretikes it is not ſo, where euery one of them is a diuerſe maiſter, and teacheth contrarie to the other, and wil be called Rabbi and Maiſter, euery one of their owne Diſciples: Arius a Rabbi among the Arians, Luther among the Lutherans, and among the Caluiniſts Caluin.

annotations.title: Maiſters.
annotations.text: [1] Wiclefe and the like Heretics of this time do herevpon condemne degrees of Schole and titles of Doctors and Maſters: where they might as wel reproue S. Paul for calling himſelf Doctor and Maſter of the Gentiles [2] : and for ſaying [3] that there ſhould be always Doctors in the Church. And whereas they bring the other words folowing, againſt Religious men who are called Fathers: as wel might they by this place take away the name of carnal fathers, and blame S. Paul for calling himſelf the only ſpiritual Father of the Corinthians [4]. But indeed nothing is here forbidden but the contentious diuiſion and partiality of ſuch as make themſelves Ringleaders of Schiſms and Sects, as Donatus, Arius, Luther, Caluin.

annotations.title: Scribes and Phariſees.
annotations.text: ◦ In al theſe reprehenſions it is much to be noted, that our Sauiour for the honour of Prieſthod neuer reprehendeth Prieſts by that name. Cypr. ep. 65. Whereas our Heretikes vſe this name of purpoſe in reproche and deſpite.

annotations.title: Praying long prayers.
annotations.text: ◦ They are not reprehended here for the things them ſelues, which for the moſt part are good, as, long prayer, making Proſelytes, garniſhing the Prophetes ſepulchres, &c. but for their wicked purpoſe and intention, as before is ſaid of faſting, prayers, almes, Mat. 6.

annotations.title: Double more.
annotations.text: ◦ They that teach that it is ynough to haue only faith, doe make ſuch Chriſtians, as the Iewes did Proſelytes, children of Hel far more then before. Auguſt. lib. de fide & oper. cap. 26.

annotations.title: Sanctifieth.
annotations.text: Note that donaries and gifts beſtowed vpon Churches and altars, be ſanctified by dedication to God, and by touching the altar and other holy things: as now ſpecially the veſſels of the ſacrifice and Sacrament of Chriſtes body and bloud, by touching the ſame, [1] and the altar it ſelf wherevpon it is conſecrated. Whereof Theophylacte [2] writeth thus vpon this place: In the old lavv Chriſt permitteth not the gift to be greater then the altar, but with vs, the altar is ſanctified by the gift: for the hoſtes by the diuine grace are turned into our Lords body, and therfore is the altar alſo ſanctified by them.

notes.text: The altar is sanctified by our Lords body therevpon.

annotations.title: By him that dwelleth therein.
annotations.text: By this we ſee that ſwearing by creatures, as by the Goſpel, by Saincts, is al referred to the honour of God, whoſe Goſpel it is, whoſe Saincts they are.

annotations.title: Appeare to men.
annotations.text: Chriſt might boldly reprehend them ſo often aud ſo vehemently for hypocriſie, becauſe he knew their harts and intentions: but we that can not ſee within men, may not preſume to call mens external good doings, hypocriſie, but iudge of men as we ſee and know.

annotations.title: Garniſh.
annotations.text: Chriſt blameth not the Iewes for adorning the ſepulchres of the Prophetes, but entwyteth them of their malice toward him, and of that which by his diuine knowledge he foreſaw, that they would accompliſh the wickednes of their fathers in ſheding his bloud, as their fathers did the bloud of the Prophetes. Hilar.
